problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -2 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,c=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 5\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem:
Calculate the volume of the $4$-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by the vectors

$$
a=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,c=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 5 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,d=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's construct the matrix $M,$ whose columns are the coordinates of our vectors $a,$ $b,$ $c,$ and  $d:$

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by these vectors equals the absolute value of the determinant of $M:$

$$
V=|det(M)|
$$

Notice that the $2$nd row of the determinant contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 5 & 4 \\ 4 & 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 5 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 5 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $3$rd row of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(M) & =-2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 5 & 4 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot 3\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-6|\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 5 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-6(4-25) \\  & =126.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume is

$$
V=|det(M)|=|126|=126.
$$
